comparable_cases.why_comparable: Active Place of Entertainment permit at 998 Valencia (Amados), 31 meters away, same NCT-Valencia zoning district. Entertainment permit shows live performance is approved on the immediate block.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: POE permit directly across the street demonstrates that live entertainment is principally permitted accessory to a restaurant use in NCT-Valencia and the Entertainment Commission approves such permits on this block. Operators must still meet soundproofing and Good Neighbor Policy conditions.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Agency referral (Planning's response to Entertainment Commission) for the POE at 998 Valencia in 2014. NCT-Valencia district, approved live entertainment accessory to retail use limited to 1/3 of gross floor area per Police Code Section 1060(r).
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Planning approved the POE at 998 Valencia as accessory entertainment under Planning Code 703.2(b)(1)(C)(viii), subject to a floor-area cap. A standalone bar with live entertainment (not accessory to retail) will require a full CUA, not just an agency referral.

comparable_cases.permit_type: Place of Entertainment, Extended Hours Premises
comparable_cases.why_comparable: Active POE and Extended Hours Premises permit at 2500 Mission (Hidden Frequency), 145 meters away in NCT-Mission district. Late-night live entertainment venue approved by the Entertainment Commission.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Demonstrates that late-night entertainment venues are achievable on the Mission corridor within 500 feet of the subject site. The concept's 1 am close is earlier and will not trigger extended-hours requirements, making approval more straightforward.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: CUA application for a bar within a full-service restaurant at 970-974 Valencia, 66 meters away in NCT-Valencia. Filed 2010, withdrawn 2011.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Withdrawal of a bar-in-restaurant CUA application on Valencia shows that bar-use CUAs face scrutiny even when presented as accessory to food service. The record does not state why the applicant withdrew, but it flags that bar CUAs are not rubber-stamped in NCT-Valencia.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: CUA application for a Type 41 beer-and-wine restaurant with live entertainment at 2519 Mission, 210 meters away in NCT-Mission. Filed 2019, withdrawn 2019.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Withdrawal of a CUA for a restaurant with Type 41 and live entertainment signals potential challenges for food-and-entertainment hybrids. The applicant withdrew before the hearing; the record does not state why, but the concept is similar to the proposed bar.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Agency referral at 1007 Valencia, 45 meters away in NCT-Valencia, approved 2008 for continuation of an existing Type 41 license. Planning explicitly noted 'Approval does not establish a new bar use at subject location.'
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Planning's 2008 language distinguishing continuation of a restaurant license from establishing a new bar use confirms that converting a restaurant to a bar (rather than renewing an existing license) is a material change requiring CUA review, consistent with the Mission SUD rules.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: CUA approved 1999 for outdoor activity area in conjunction with a full-service restaurant/bar at 2526-2548 Mission, 159 meters away in NCT-Mission. Use decision approving a bar component within a restaurant.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: NCT-Mission approved a full-service restaurant/bar CUA in 1999, showing that bars accessory to restaurant uses can receive CUA approval on the Mission corridor. The current concept is a standalone bar, which is a more intensive use than a restaurant with bar service.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Agency referral at 2519 Mission (210 meters, NCT-Mission) approved in 2021 for Public Convenience or Necessity recommendation for a nonprofit theater with accessory bar, in an undue-concentration census tract.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Planning approved a PCN referral for a bar use in an undue-concentration area on Mission Street. Demonstrates Planning will support bar uses that meet PCN criteria (public benefit, no undue impact), though this was accessory to a theater, not a standalone bar.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: CUA approved in 2007 at 2410-2412 Mission (193 meters, NCT-Mission) to change from an existing bar use to a retail store. Use decision confirms a bar use existed and was approved for conversion.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Approval of a CUA to convert a bar to retail demonstrates that the Mission corridor has a history of bar uses in NCT-Mission. Conversion away from bar use rather than toward it provides no positive signal for a new bar, but confirms bars were historically permitted.

filing_playbook.action: Engage a licensed liquor-license broker to locate an ABC Type 42 license from a bar within the Mission SUD and open escrow.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: The Mission Alcoholic Beverage SUD requires the license to come from another bar inside the district boundaries. Confirm with the broker that the source bar is within the SUD polygon and that ABC has no outstanding violations or protests on the source license. Make the lease contingent on securing the license.

filing_playbook.what_to_say: Explain the concept as a neighborhood wine bar with small plates and live acoustic music, closing at 1 am—earlier and less intensive than nearby late-night venues. Ask Planning to confirm the license must come from within the SUD and what operating conditions are likely. Request guidance on the Good Neighbor Policy before filing.

timeline_cost.notes: The critical path is the Conditional Use Authorization (120–300 days, $3,100–$15,000 per catalog:sf.conditional_use_authorization) followed by the ABC Type 42 license transfer (60–150 days, $1,000–$1,600 per catalog:ca.abc_type_42). The Mission SUD license-transfer requirement adds 1–3 months to locate and escrow a qualifying license, and the undue-concentration flag may trigger a Public Convenience or Necessity process adding another 60–90 days. The Place of Entertainment permit (45–120 days, $2,708–$3,800 per catalog:sf.place_of_entertainment_permit) can run in parallel with the building permit (14–120 days, $800–$15,000 per catalog:sf.building_permit) after CUA approval. Health plan check and permit add 35–105 days and $1,298–$3,500 (catalog:sf.health_plan_check, catalog:sf.health_permit). Minor costs include business registration ($55–$700), sign permit ($300–$1,500), entity formation ($70–$150), food safety certifications ($100–$250), RBS training ($3–$30 per employee) and music licenses ($600–$5,000 annually). The timeline assumes no significant delays from neighbor appeals, incomplete plans or failed inspections. Budget 8–18 months from lease signature to opening, with government fees of $8,500–$24,000 not including construction, rent, insurance, legal or the license purchase price.

status_definitions.allowed: Allowed: the cited records or code sections show this approval is available as of right, or already exists for this space, without a discretionary hearing.
status_definitions.further_review: Further review: the approval is obtainable only through a discretionary or multi-step review (a hearing, a referral, a licence investigation) whose result the records do not settle.
status_definitions.potential_blocker: Potential blocker: a cited rule, cap or record could stop this approval or force a change to the concept unless a specific condition is met.
status_definitions.not_permitted: Not permitted: a cited code section prohibits this use or approval at this address as the concept is described.
status_definitions.insufficient_information: Insufficient information: the records in hand do not show whether this approval is needed or obtainable; the could-not-establish section says what would settle it.

confidence_definitions.verified: Verified: stated directly by a cited record or code section that applies to this exact address, parcel or zoning district.
confidence_definitions.likely_applicable: Likely applicable: inferred from cited records of comparable cases or from a general rule; not stated for this address.
confidence_definitions.needs_confirmation: Needs confirmation: plausible but not supported by a record in hand; confirm with the agency or document named.
confidence_definitions.professional_review_required: Professional review required: depends on plans, an inspection, or legal or design judgment that public records cannot supply.

records_summary: The property at 995 Valencia St currently operates as Sarita's Grill & Beer with an active Type 41 beer-and-wine restaurant license issued in November 2023. The records show a continuous restaurant use since at least 1999, with the space upgrading from a Type 41 to Type 47 full-bar license in 2011 before reverting to Type 41 in 2023. The concept will require a Conditional Use Authorization because it is a bar use (not a restaurant) in the NCT-Valencia district and falls within the Mission Alcoholic Beverage Special Use District, which permits new bars only with a CU and requires the liquor license to be transferred from another bar within the SUD. The block is extremely active with 24 food/drink businesses and 9 active on-sale ABC licenses within 500 feet; ABC's undue-concentration flag is raised, likely requiring a Public Convenience or Necessity finding. Only 3 comparable use decisions were recorded nearby in the past 10 years—too few to establish an approval rate—though 74 entertainment permits and licenses were granted in that radius.
